editorial.headline: Clearing’s Counterparty: KBLI 64993 and Bali’s PMA Position
editorial.standfirst: A financial-market counterparty activity open to foreign ownership nationally and not blocked from PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 64993 covers the activity of a party that places itself between participants in financial transactions: buyer to the seller, and seller to the buyer. Its terrain is the machinery of clearing and settlement across capital markets, commodity futures, digital financial assets including crypto assets, money markets, foreign-exchange markets, and other financial markets. It also includes the provision of clearing services and guarantees for exchange transactions to be completed in an orderly, fair and efficient manner; PT Kliring Penjaminan Efek Indonesia is expressly included within the stated scope.

This is therefore not merely an administrative description of post-trade processing. The activity is defined by an intermediary position at the centre of a transaction, taking on the role of counterparty on both sides while supporting its clearing and settlement. The record makes the breadth of the remit clear: it reaches established market venues as well as financial markets involving digital assets, without reducing the activity to any one asset class or trading environment.

Registration is open across every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. At the national level, PMA is classified TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling stands at 100%. Put simply, the national record allows full foreign ownership for this activity. That openness is grounded in Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021, the sources identified in the record.

Bali’s position is equally important, and more favourable than a blanket reading of the province’s PMA moratorium might suggest. Bali permanently blocks PMA registration for all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities island-wide. KBLI 64993 is not blocked by that moratorium: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, and the Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. For an investor considering Bali, the honest conclusion is straightforward: this activity is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership and is not barred from PMA registration in Bali under the stated moratorium rule.
